instruction:
Use NIST HTML guidance on writing SI units, metric prefixes, SP 811 Chapters 4, 6 and 7, and SP 330 Section 4. Build a six-row editorial checklist correcting these fictional expressions while preserving each quantity: 5 kgs, 10m, 25 degrees Kelvin, 0.8 mms, 4 sec and 2 microkilograms. State the rule behind each correction, including spacing, plural symbols, kelvin notation and the kilogram prefix exception. Separately convert 2.5 square centimetres to square millimetres, 3 cubic centimetres to millilitres, 1500 milligrams to grams, 72 kilometres per hour to metres per second, 1.8 litres to cubic centimetres, and 120 kilopascals to pascals. Treat the inputs as exact, show conversion factors and explain why powers of a prefixed unit must also apply to its scale factor. Compare the currently listed extreme SI prefixes and the year the newest four were added, using the prefix table rather than an older count. Distinguish unit symbols, quantity symbols and unit names, and note the publication/update context of the guidance used. Cite the relevant written rules and tables; do not open PDF editions.

Stopping condition: Stop when six cited notation corrections and six factor-based conversions are supplied, with prefix-power reasoning, the current extreme prefixes and their addition year, and source publication context.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.description: Full credit if the agent correctly identifies the correction to '5 kg' and states the rule regarding plural symbols for units.
Full credit if the agent correctly identifies the correction to '10 m' and states the rule regarding spacing between the numerical value and unit symbol.
Full credit if the agent correctly identifies the correction to '25 K' and states the rule regarding kelvin notation (no degree symbol).
Full credit if the agent correctly identifies the correction to '0.8 mm' and states the rule regarding plural symbols for units.
Full credit if the agent correctly identifies the correction to '4 s' and states the rule regarding the use of proper symbols instead of abbreviations.
Full credit if the agent correctly identifies the correction to '2 mg' and states the rule regarding the kilogram prefix exception (only one prefix, applied to the gram name/symbol).

items.criterion: Convert 2.5 square centimetres to square millimetres
items.description: Full credit if the agent correctly converts 2.5 cm^2 to 250 mm^2 and explicitly shows the exact conversion factor used.
Full credit if the agent correctly converts 3 cm^3 to 3 mL and explicitly shows the exact conversion factor used (1 cm^3 = 1 mL).
Full credit if the agent correctly converts 1500 mg to 1.5 g and explicitly shows the exact conversion factor used.

items.criterion: Convert 72 kilometres per hour to metres per second
items.description: Full credit if the agent correctly converts 72 km/h to 20 m/s and explicitly shows the exact conversion factor used.
Full credit if the agent correctly converts 1.8 L to 1800 cm^3 and explicitly shows the exact conversion factor used.
Full credit if the agent correctly converts 120 kPa to 120,000 Pa and explicitly shows the exact conversion factor used.

Full credit for accurately explaining why powers of a prefixed unit must also apply to its scale factor (e.g., that a power applied to a unit symbol applies to the whole symbol, including the prefix).

items.criterion: Identify extreme SI prefixes and their addition year
items.description: Full credit if the agent compares the extreme SI prefixes currently displayed during the run and states the documented addition year of the newest four, citing the HTML prefix table rather than relying on an older prefix count.

items.criterion: Distinguish unit symbols, quantity symbols, and unit names
items.description: Full credit if the agent accurately distinguishes between unit symbols, quantity symbols, and unit names as defined in the NIST guidance.

items.criterion: Note context and cite HTML sources without using PDFs
items.description: Full credit if the agent notes the publication/update context of the NIST guidance used and cites the relevant written rules and tables from the HTML pages, explicitly avoiding the opening or use of PDF editions.
